headline: Fewer jobs, new opportunities: AI is changing what's in store for new hires and managers alike
claim: AI résumé screening is leading managers to hire fewer entry-level workers.
notes: published 2026-11-02; university's own AI & Society Survey of 8,174 people involved in hiring decisions. Northeastern is the source of the survey. Survey of managers' reported behavior, not a measured hiring count. Same article says other managers expect newcomers to do more advanced work.

headline: Kids Hooked on AI Chatbots Are Showing Dramatically Worse Mental Health
claim: Young people who use AI chatbots during emotional distress have worse mental health and more suicidal thoughts and attempts.
notes: published 2026-11-05; reports the JED Foundation's AI and Mental Health Report 2026, a mental health advocacy group's own survey. Sample size not stated in the article. Correlational; the article does not establish cause. Same study as the NPR-syndicated OPB and LPM rows.

headline: AI Rebounding: Companies that Cut Jobs Are Now Asking Workers to Come Back
claim: Workers laid off because of AI are being asked back, which suggests the AI-driven layoffs were a mistake.
notes: published 2026-11-03; SHL survey (SHL is a talent assessment company, so an interested party), fielded June-July 2026 by Propeller Insights, over 1,000 US and 1,000 UK workers. The article does not say the survey found the layoffs a mistake; that framing comes from an SHL executive quoted in the piece.

headline: Nearly 1 in 5 workers laid off due to AI are asked to return, survey finds
claim: Workers laid off because of AI are being asked back, which suggests the AI-driven layoffs were a mistake.
notes: published 2026-11-02; same SHL survey as the CNBC row (SHL is a talent assessment company, an interested party; fielded by Propeller Insights June-July 2026). Survey does not itself say the layoffs were a mistake.
